name: Ngatik Men's Creole
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: Tryon, Darrell, 'Ngatikese Men's Language', pp. 345-357; and Tryon & Charpentier (2004), Pacific Pidgins and Creoles.
earlier_scan.note: Short descriptions of Ngatik Men's Creole exist; none reachable online; stress coverage uncertain

sources.note: No descriptive references; endangerment note from Rentz 2014 p.c. Alternative names Ngatikese, Micronesian Pidgin, Ngatik Men's Language.

sources.citation: Lee, Nala H. 2018. Contact languages around the world and their levels of endangerment. Language Documentation & Conservation 12: 53-79
sources.note: Nothing; vitality tables only (Ngatik Men's Creole 15-30 speakers, severely endangered).

sources.citation: Rentz, Bradley T. 2018. Pohnpei sohte ehu: a survey- and interview-based approach to language attitudes on Pohnpei. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Manoa. hdl 10125/62508
sources.note: Nothing on the creole (Ngatikese appears only as a community). §3.7.1 p.58 says of Pohnpeian: 'Pohnpeian does not have lexical stress, but rather seems to mark prominence via intonational boundary tones (Rentz & Anderson under review)' — a statement about Pohnpeian (pohn1238), not about ngat1248.

sources.citation: Rentz, Bradley. 2014. Kaipuleohone deposit BR1: BR1-004 word list and example sentences in Ngatik Men's Creole (Remikio Frank); BR1-009 conversation (21:50). University of Hawai'i at Manoa
sources.note: Open primary audio; the only route to a first-hand stress statement for the creole is an instrumental/auditory study of these recordings (word list is 2 min 15 s).

sources.citation: Tryon, Darrell T. 2001. Ngatikese Men's Language. In Andrew Pawley, Malcolm Ross & Darrell Tryon (eds), The boy from Bundaberg: studies in Melanesian linguistics in honour of Tom Dutton, 345-359. Canberra: Pacific Linguistics (PL 514). DOI 10.15144/PL-514.345
sources.note: Nothing. The paper has sections 1 Introduction (history of the 1837 massacre), 2 Ngatikese Pidgin morphosyntax (2.1 pronouns.. 2.9 non-verbal sentences), 3 Ngatikese Pidgin and Pacific pidgins, 4 two texts. The only phonological remarks are footnotes on p.348: fn 2 'In standard Ponapean orthography, followed here, /h/ following a vowel indicates a long vowel'; fn 4 'In Ngatikese Pidgin, orthographic rh = [x]'. a full-text search for stress/accent the full text for stress/accent/prosod/intonation/syllable/phonolog returns no hit.
sources.venue: The boy from Bundaberg: studies in Melanesian linguistics in honour of Tom Dutton

sources.citation: Wurm, Stephen A., Peter Mühlhäusler & Darrell T. Tryon (eds). 1996. Atlas of Languages of Intercultural Communication in the Pacific, Asia, and the Americas. Berlin: Mouton de Gruyter
sources.note: Google Books snippet of the Ngatik entry: '..Ngatikese creole has appeared in published form. Its genesis and current status and use is, however, of considerable interest..' (i.e. the Atlas itself reports that no description had been published).

sources.citation: Dutton, Tom, Malcolm Ross & Darrell Tryon (eds). 1992. The language game: papers in memory of Donald C. Laycock. Pacific Linguistics C-110 (688 pp.)
sources.note: Irrelevant: downloaded because the scan's 'pp. 345-357' pointer had no volume; the TOC shows Tryon's chapter here is 'Whence the Jolly Jumbuck?' and pp. 345-357 are Platt/Putz chapters. No Ngatik content (no 'gatik' in the 20k-line text).

sources.citation: Mühlhäusler, Peter. 1985. The number of Pidgin Englishes in the Pacific. Papers in Pidgin and Creole Linguistics 4, 25-51. Pacific Linguistics A-72
sources.note: Only names 'Ngatik Men's Language' in Clark's (1980) family tree of Pacific pidgins; no description.
sources.venue: Papers in Pidgin and Creole Linguistics

sources.note: Pronoun table and text copied from Tryon 2001 under CC BY-SA; gives the Kaipuleohone handles; no phonology. Identifies the non-creole Ngatikese as Glottolog sapw1237.

sources.citation: Tryon, Darrell T. & Jean-Michel Charpentier. 2004. Pacific Pidgins and Creoles: origins, growth and development. Berlin: Mouton de Gruyter. Ch. 2 'Present-day Pacific pidgins' pp. 5-20 (Ngatikese at p. 14) and ch. 10 pp. 401-478

sources.citation: Rehg, Kenneth L. 1979. A linguistic history of Ngatikese. MS, 5th Annual Oceanic Festival, University of Hawai'i (cited in Tryon 2001: 359); plus Rehg's Ngatik field notes lent to Tryon
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Rehg is the Pohnpeic phonologist (cf. Rehg 1993 'Proto-Micronesian prosody' in Tonality in Austronesian Languages, which discusses Ngatikese dialect prosody); his Ngatikese material is the likeliest place a prosodic remark on Ngatik speech exists, though it concerns the dialect (sapw1237) rather than the creole.
